key_insight: Wall curvature reorganizes supersonic turbulence: concave walls promote multi-step triadic energy transfers and vortex breakdown, while convex walls suppress redistribution and retain energy in elongated streamwise streaks.
engineering_relevance: Separating nonlinear scale selection from linear flow-structure amplification can inform turbulence modeling for curved supersonic surfaces.
method: Direct numerical simulations of supersonic boundary layers over concave and convex walls.
Scale-resolved TKE budgets, triadic-transfer bispectra, and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition.
Global resolvent analysis to identify linear receptivity and convective amplification.
evidence_signal: DNS-based diagnostics identify a concave-wall outer-layer production peak at low spanwise wavenumbers and convex-wall suppression of pressure fluctuations and pressure-strain redistribution.
watch_item: Generality across Mach numbers, Reynolds numbers, and curvature strengths is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Triadic energy cascades and linear amplification mechanisms in supersonic turbulent boundary layers over curved walls
